adjudication_u3.ch_reason: The ODS ORD API confirms RXF is MID YORKSHIRE TEACHING NHS TRUST, Active RO197, operational since 2002-04-01 with no successors. The only Mid Yorkshire RO197 body ODS returns is RXF; 'MID YORKSHIRE HOSPITALS NHS TRUST' appears only as AFYR, an Inactive RO104 non-trust entry. So 'Mid Yorkshire Hospitals NHS Trust' is the same code's pre-rename name, not a predecessor or successor body. 30917291 is the code's PPON org, PTPB4248VJQT, carrying both the old name (27 mentions) and the new name (3); it is SAME. 31539005 has 45 mentions under the exact current name, 6 coded; it is SAME. Both pass the census's structural checks: admitted, no denials. However, 30917291 has key_owners_elsewhere=[6724930]: a standing identifier-NULL GB row outside the body owns its head-name key 'mid yorkshire hospitals nhs trust'. The census marks this status 'member-key-owned-elsewhere', and D4 holds the member. Dropping 30917291 would make the provisional cluster the survivor in place of the PPON org (D1), so holding is correct. A human should look at 6724930, which is likely the trust's uncoded old-name twin. Same members and decision as the reviewer.
